summary: Slice TF-020P-005 introduces scripts/scp-pre-push-verify.sh as an informational local-dev wrapper. No CRIT or MAJ safety findings. The wrapper is correctly scoped as informational only (CI is the authoritative gate) and introduces no new bypass surface: the three CI gates it mirrors are read-only operations with no enforcement claim, CODEOWNERS scripts/** @jrnb2024 covers the wrapper path, and threshold-90 is a hardcoded literal not subject to env-var override. Two MIN findings require inline fixes before merge: (MIN-SAFE-001) the version-drift warning understates the likelihood of CI rejection for large version gaps, and (MIN-SAFE-002) ADOPT-001 §12.7.9.1 lacks an explicit statement that the section is for SCP-repo rule authors only, leaving adopters who read §12.7.9 susceptible to misapplying the wrapper. Two nit findings are filed for completeness. No descoping recommended; both MINs have one-line or one-sentence fixes.

findings.claim: The version-drift warning emitted when local opa/regal versions diverge from scripts/.tool-versions uses the phrasing 'local results may diverge', which understates the probability of CI rejection when the version gap is large (e.g., regal 0.30.0 vs CI-pinned 0.40.0). A developer who sees 'may diverge' may reasonably continue and push, only to discover CI fails — the exact CI-roundtrip-waste the wrapper was designed to prevent.
findings.evidence: scripts/scp-pre-push-verify.sh line 109: emit_warn "${tool}: pinned ${pinned} (scripts/.tool-versions) but local ${installed} — CI uses pinned; local results may diverge". The phrase 'may diverge' is correct when versions are close but misleading when the gap spans multiple minor releases (e.g., regal 0.30.0 lacks rules that 0.40.0 introduces by default). The warning is non-fatal by documented design (DISPATCH-NOTE Risk #1), which is the correct policy, but the message text does not communicate that a push will likely fail CI if the version gap is significant.
findings.impact: A developer running regal 0.30.0 against CI-pinned 0.40.0 gets a false-passing wrapper verdict on newly-introduced lint rules. They push; CI fails. The wrapper's stated purpose — saving CI roundtrips — is defeated. The warning is the only signal, but 'may diverge' does not convey urgency. This is MIN (not MAJ) because CI remains authoritative and the wrapper header explicitly states 'CI is still the authoritative gate'; the failure mode is wasted time, not a security bypass.
findings.mitigation: Tighten the warning text to convey that divergence is likely, not merely possible, and that the developer should verify with the CI-pinned version before relying on the result. Proposed replacement for line 109: emit_warn "${tool}: local ${installed} differs from CI-pinned ${pinned} (scripts/.tool-versions) — wrapper results may not match CI; install the pinned version or treat wrapper output as advisory only". One-line change, no structural impact.

findings.claim: ADOPT-001 §12.7.9.1 is nested under §12.7.9 ('Pre-commit hook (optional, recommended)'), which is an adopter-facing section that includes strong SHA-pinning language ('The local SCP clone MUST be checked out at the same commit SHA as your wrapper\'s # tag: pin'). §12.7.9.1 introduces a different tool (scripts/scp-pre-push-verify.sh) for a different audience (SCP-repo rule authors), but does not explicitly disclaim applicability to adopter clones. An adopter reading §12.7.9 may read §12.7.9.1, attempt to wire scripts/scp-pre-push-verify.sh into their pre-commit hook, and be confused when it silently succeeds (no policies/SCP-R-*.rego files in their repo → 'nothing to verify' → exit 0).
findings.evidence: docs/adoption/ADOPT-001-project-onboarding.md §12.7.9.1 (lines 1012-1020): the section opens 'If you are authoring or modifying SCP-R-NNN rule files (policies/SCP-R-*.rego)' which implies SCP-repo scope, but never states 'this section does not apply to adopter repos'. The parent §12.7.9 SHA-pinning warning (lines 1003-1010) — 'The local SCP clone MUST be checked out at the same commit SHA' — is addressed to adopters using scp-policy-check from a local SCP clone; it does not apply to §12.7.9.1 (which is run FROM the SCP repo, not from an adopter clone), but no boundary marker separates the two contexts. A developer reading top-to-bottom through §12.7.9 into §12.7.9.1 encounters no explicit scope break.
findings.impact: An adopter who runs scripts/scp-pre-push-verify.sh in their own repo gets exit 0 'nothing to verify' (because their repo has no policies/SCP-R-*.rego files). This is a silent false-pass from the adopter's perspective: they believe they ran a meaningful gate when they did not. No security bypass is introduced (the wrapper is informational and CI is authoritative), but adopter confusion could result in misplaced trust. Inline-fix is a single sentence addition to §12.7.9.1.
findings.mitigation: Add an explicit scope clarifier at the start of §12.7.9.1. Proposed addition after the heading: 'This section is for SCP-repo rule authors working directly in the standards-control-plane repository. Adopter repos do not need this wrapper — your pre-push verification is covered by the CI gate configured in §12.7.1.' One sentence, no structural change.

findings.claim: The wrapper resolves opa, regal, git, find, awk, basename, and tr from PATH. A developer who installs a shadow binary earlier in PATH than the legitimate install (e.g., ~/bin/opa pointing to a trojanised binary) would receive incorrect wrapper results. This is theoretical local-machine compromise, outside the SCP threat model.
findings.evidence: scripts/scp-pre-push-verify.sh lines 58-65: require_cmd uses command -v to resolve tools from PATH. Lines 68-69 confirm opa and regal are PATH-resolved, not SHA-verified. This is intentional — the script's DISPATCH-NOTE explicitly places SHA-verified binary bootstrapping out of scope ('Bootstrapping opa/regal binaries with SHA verification: OUT. scripts/scp-policy-check is the canonical SHA-verifying bootstrap script'). SECURITY.md scope includes 'runner-side compromise affecting the OPA/Conftest/Regal binary chain' but in the context of the CI workflow, not local developer machines.
findings.mitigation: No action required — PATH-resolution of local binaries is the documented design. The DISPATCH-NOTE correctly scopes SHA-verification to scripts/scp-policy-check. If local SHA-pinning is ever desired (e.g., for regulated developer environments), it should be a separate TF with a dedicated scope discussion, not retrofitted here. Flag retained for audit trail completeness.

findings.claim: The Gate 3 glob (line 196: for rule_file in "${POLICIES_DIR}"/SCP-R-*.rego) does not set the nullglob shell option. If no SCP-R-*.rego files exist, bash returns the literal unexpanded pattern as rule_file. The [ -e "${rule_file}" ] || continue guard on line 197 handles this correctly (the literal path does not exist; the iteration is skipped; rule_count stays 0). No incorrect behavior results. Nit filed to confirm the guard's intent is understood.
findings.evidence: scripts/scp-pre-push-verify.sh line 196-197: the guard [ -e "${rule_file}" ] || continue explicitly handles the no-match case. Line 223-225: the rule_count == 0 branch emits 'no policies/SCP-R-*.rego rules found; skipping per-rule coverage'. The behavior is correct; the pattern is a well-known bash idiom. In the SCP repo the policies/ directory will always contain SCP-R-*.rego files, making the no-match path unreachable in normal operation.
findings.mitigation: No action required. The guard is correct and the behavior is documented by the no-match emission. Optionally add a brief inline comment on line 197 noting why the guard exists ('handles no-glob-match case'), but this is cosmetic only.

self_reported_concerns: The two MIN findings (MIN-SAFE-001, MIN-SAFE-002) have simple one-line or one-sentence fixes. Neither requires structural change to the script or significant ADOPT-001 revision. If the orchestrator determines both fixes can be applied in this same slice rather than a separate fix-round, the review would reach APPROVED.

The bypass-surface analysis for tampered local opa/regal binaries (dispatch checklist item 1a) confirms the wrapper correctly disclaims authority: the script header line 25-26 states 'CI is still the authoritative gate. This wrapper is a CI-roundtrip saver for rule-author work, not a federation-conformance gate.' ADOPT-001 §12.7.9.1 end-of-paragraph repeats 'CI is still the authoritative gate' in bold. The disclaimer is present and adequate.
The threshold-90 literal (dispatch checklist item 3) is confirmed at line 216: --threshold 90 is a hardcoded string, not a variable expansion. No env var override path exists. This finding is PASS.

The find -print0 / read -r -d '' pipeline (Gate 2, lines 170-174) correctly handles filenames with spaces, newlines, and shell metacharacters. opa fmt is invoked with the filename double-quoted (line 171: opa fmt --fail "${rego_file}"). Maliciously-named .rego files cannot escape into shell evaluation through this path.
Concurrency analysis: the wrapper has no temp files, no state writes, no lock files. Concurrent runs in the same checkout are read-only and non-interfering. PASS.
Information disclosure analysis: the wrapper emits REPO_ROOT-relative paths (POLICIES_DIR, COMMON_FILE, test_file) to stderr. No env vars, SSH keys, or paths outside REPO_ROOT are emitted. PASS.

Repo-root escape: git rev-parse --show-toplevel returns the worktree root in a linked worktree (correct for the script's purpose). No files are written outside REPO_ROOT. No symlink-following write operations. PASS.
